author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 겨울철새, 해마다 수십 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 우리나라에서는 해마다 수십 마리가 겨울을 나는 드문 겨울철새로, 얕은 호수와 논, 하구, 간석지에 찾아온다. 짠물과 민물이 만나는 곳에서 부리를 수면과 나란히 둔 채 좌우로 저어 갑각류나 물속 곤충 따위를 잡는다. 유럽, 아시아, 중국에서 번식하며, 아프리카에는 따로 떨어져 사는 번식 집단이 있다.

points.en: black crown and sides of head

art.subject: Pied Avocet (Recurvirostra avosetta), adult as seen in Korean estuaries in winter (the black-and-white pattern is the same all year): cap from the forehead over the eye to the nape and the whole hindneck black; face below the eye, throat, foreneck and underparts white; on the upperparts a black stripe along the scapulars and a black band across the median wing coverts on white, giving a pied back; primaries black; tertials and tail white. Bill black, long, needle-thin and curving strongly upward in its outer half; dark eye; long blue-grey legs with partly webbed toes.
art.pose: wading in shallow brackish water, sweeping its bill from side to side at the surface
art.scene: Korean estuary where a river meets the sea, shallow water over tidal flats; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view wading in shallow water: black cap and hindneck, white face and body, black scapular stripe and black wing-covert bar on the folded wing, black primaries, long thin upcurved black bill, long blue-grey legs
adult, head detail: black cap reaching down to the eye, white face and throat, long, needle-thin black bill curving upward in its outer half to a fine point
art.build: Elegant, slender wader, about 43cm long, clearly larger than Common Redshank and smaller than Eurasian Curlew; small rounded head on a fairly long neck. Bill much longer than the head, needle-thin, nearly straight at the base and curving strongly upward in the outer half to a fine point. Legs long and blue-grey, toes partly webbed; often swims. At rest the black wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight black outer wing, black scapular stripes and black covert bars on white; legs project beyond the tail.
avoid: Do not paint a straight or downcurved bill; the bill curves strongly upward.
Do not paint red or pink legs — that is Black-winged Stilt (Himantopus himantopus); avocet legs are blue-grey.
Do not paint an all-white back; the black scapular stripe and wing-covert bar are always present.
Do not paint a black face or throat; the black is limited to the cap and hindneck.
